text:
jordan: FYI, FinEdge (hosted) opened a ticket: sudden p99 regressions + some 502s on chat endpoint since ~11:05 UTC. Their SLA-sensitive routes are impacted. Can runtime/SRE look?

lee: saw our alert: synthetic check for redwood-large-2 had p95 go from 280ms -> 620ms and p99 jumped to ~2.1s. Error rate increased from 0.02% -> 0.8%.

rachael: any recent infra changes? dev-bot: deploy pushed at 03:10 had param "gpu_allocator=cuda_async" flipped on a canary subset. Also autoscaler tuning for pool 'prod-gpu-03' rolled at 09:00.

jordan: customer says failures mostly after long conversations, sequences ~700 tokens, and they use KV retention=900s. They also batch at 16. support-bot posted sample curl and timestamps.

lee: grabbing NVML and runtime logs now. Initial look: GPUs show high transient mem fragmentation, free drops to ~200MB during peaks, but no hard OOM. Kernel-side I/O stalls visible (cudaMemcpySync spikes).

rachael: interesting signal: model KV entries per-session up ~22% over last hour for that tenant, and route-level batching queues show one or two requests often pinning a batch for an extra 1.5s.

jordan: so hypothesis: KV cache growth + cuda_async allocator path fragmentation -> slower allocations and memcpy stall -> batch tail dragged.

lee: reproducer run on staging with flags: `--concurrency 24 --seq 700 --kv-retention 900 --batch-size 16 --allocator cuda_async`. Observed p99 ~2.0s, median ~320ms. Swap allocator to `gpu_alloc_basic` and p99 drops to 480ms.

rachael: we haven't tested shard-level KV eviction. Could be accumulation of many small KV blobs that cause the GPU-side allocator to fragment. Also cuda_async uses deferred free which can spike when it drains.

jordan: immediate mitigations suggested: 1) toggle back allocator flag on affected nodes, 2) reduce tenant KV retention to 180s for FinEdge, 3) lower per-route max batch to 8 and set batch_timeout=8ms, 4) scale up pool by 2 nodes as short-term capacity. Any objections?

lee: +1 to revert allocator on prod-gpu-03 canaries. I'll start revert job.

rachael: I'll push KV retention override and batch size change via routing config for FinEdge at 11:30. ops-bot: change queued.

ops-bot: revert-allocator-prod-gpu-03 started at 11:33 UTC on 2 nodes.

lee: revert completed 11:39 UTC. Verified `gpu_allocator=cuda_async` removed.

rachael: KV retention override and batch changes applied at 11:41 UTC. Also added per-tenant eviction threshold to 256MB.

jordan: synthetic after mitigations: p95 0.34s, p99 0.55s, error rate back to 0.03%. NVML shows free mem up to ~1.0GB and memcpy stall traces resolved.

support-bot: FinEdge confirmed improved performance and dropped complaints. They saw brief 502s while we toggled routing but all good now.

lee: follow-ups: add a canary test that replays long-session KV growth patterns against allocator variants. Add metric `cuda_async_drain_latency` and `kv_blob_count_per_tenant`.

rachael: ops action list:
- block further rollout of `gpu_allocator=cuda_async` until KV-heavy stress tests pass (owner: eng-runtime)
- add per-tenant KV retention override UI + API (owner: product)
- tune batching defaults to prefer smaller max_batch for routes with expected long sequences (owner: eng-sre)

jordan: I'll open incident INC-2026-458 with timeline + logs + reproducer. Please drop artifacts there.

lee: reproducible command for posterity:
```
# staging stress
python -m tools/load_test --model redwood-large-2 --concurrency 24 --seq-len 700 --kv-retention 900 --batch 16 --allocator cuda_async --duration 12m
```

rachael: also adding a short runbook note: if you see p99 > 1s with GPU free < 512MB and KV blobs trending up, consider: reduce KV retention, revert async allocator flag, and temporarily reduce batch size for the route before scaling.

jordan: great work. We'll keep this thread until postmortem doc is up.

dev-bot: incident INC-2026-458 created by jordan at 12:05 UTC.

rachael: scheduling 45-min sync tomorrow to decide whether to rework allocator drain heuristics vs keep fallback to basic allocator.

jordan: thanks all, closing slack thread once PM confirms postmortem link.
